We're hiring our first Account Executive.

Here's the story so far: we've sold 210 booths, every one of them closed by a founder. That can't scale. So we're bringing in a salesperson to help us grow.

If you want to grow with us, apply via the link in the comments.

We built a beautiful app. Nobody used it.

When we launched Rotaship, we were proud of our sleek mobile app. We figured restaurant staff would love it.

Only 12% of staff even opened it in the first month.

That stung. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding another one.

Restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025 we made the tough call and moved everything into WhatsApp.

The results: 140 outlets, and a median reply time to shift messages under 20 minutes.

Meet your users where they already are. Don't make them come to you.

Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love.

We raised our prices by 50%. Here's what happened.

In September, we made one of the scariest calls in Tabwise's history: raising our price from $8 to $12 per user per month.

Why? Our support costs per customer had doubled since launch. We could compromise on quality or charge what we're actually worth.

We chose value.

But we didn't want to leave our loyal customers behind. Every existing customer kept their $8 price for 12 months.

The result? Two out of 140 customers churned in the following 2 months.

Two.

The lesson: your customers aren't paying for software. They're paying for outcomes. Price accordingly.

Founders, when did you last raise your prices?

#SaaS #Pricing #StartupLessons #Growth #B2B

After 11 years in a clinic, I quit.

I still loved being a vet. But something kept breaking my heart.

Every day, pets came in so terrified we had to sedate them just to look in their ears.

Calmer pets. Happier owners. Better medicine.

#Veterinary #PetCare #Melbourne #Entrepreneurship #FollowYourPassion

1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we promised it would stay free for open source. People told us we were crazy. How would we make money?

Today we run on 1,200 repositories. About 900 of them are open source.

And here's the number that stopped me: across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures was a flaky test. Think about what that costs you. Hours of developer time on red builds that were never real failures.

Open source gave us more than users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers. We shipped it on November 12.

Giving back to open source is part of our strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

If you're bootstrapping and grinding through late nights, keep going. Profitability beats hype. Sustainability beats vanity metrics.

What helped you grow without funding? Tell me below.

#Startups #Portugal #Parenting #FemaleFounders #Gratitude

Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline.

5 months in, they walked away. It stung.

They had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were.

So we did what we had to do: we listened, and we spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. That work changed how we think about our customers.

Today, we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields.

The hard feedback from customers tells you what to build. You just have to listen.

Why we stopped billing by the hour and never looked back.

When we started Fernway Studio, we charged hourly, like every agency does. 4 of our first six projects ran over budget. Clients were frustrated. So were we. Trust was slipping.

So in 2024 we switched to a fixed price: KES 450,000 per Shopify store. That changed everything. Clients know what they're paying before we start. We work smarter instead of longer. Our relationships run on trust, not timesheets.

Since then we've launched 31 stores. Only 2 went past our 6-week timeline.

Pricing is a promise.

Founders, how do you price your services? Tell me in the comments.

#Entrepreneurship #Africa #Shopify #AgencyLife #Pricing

Today we completed our 100th installation at Gridline Solar.

The milestone system went on a mechanic's workshop in Mooca. Just 2 years ago we installed our very first one. Since then we've helped 100 small businesses across São Paulo switch to clean energy, every single one with R$ 0 upfront.

We promised installation in 21 days. Our average is 19.

It's about more than solar panels. It's about strengthening local businesses and communities, and building a brighter future for Brazil.

Thank you to our team and to every customer who believed in us. Here's to the next 100.

Why we walked away from the 25% recruiting fee.

For years, Northbound Talent charged what every recruiting firm charges: 25% of first-year salary. Our average fee ran about $41,000 per hire. For an early-stage startup, that's a huge bite of runway. And the model rewarded us for your salary going up, which never felt like partnership.

So in January we switched to a flat $18,000 per hire. No percentages.
